problems.detail: DB-ONLY ROW — UNDERCABINET-LIGHTING OUTLET (keynote 50) is carried on room 105 at HIGH in data/project.sqlite and the sheets do not support it. A555 views 04 / 04.1 place keynotes 3, 10, 14, 15, 16, 24, 25, 28, 36, 44, 45, 46, 47, 51 — 50 is absent. A550 line 165 defines kn50 in the LEGEND ONLY, and a legend definition is not a placement. packages/electrical.md §5.1.1 (repair CR-2, 2026-08-07) restricts kn50 to the 7 accessible keys after it had wrongly been booked on all 115: 'no sheet outside the accessible group places keynote 50.' On floor 1 that is room 118 only. Emitted as a qty-0 confirm-absent line at FLAGGED, origin db-only — not silently dropped and not silently kept as fact. FIX: clear this row from the 15 non-accessible first-floor rooms in the DB, or the crew punches 15 rooms for an outlet the drawings never placed.

DB-ONLY ROW — DOORBELL ON/OFF SWITCH (kn28, tag DB) is carried on room 105 and the sheets do not support it for this room. kn28 IS placed on A555 view 04, but A555 is the type sheet for every QQ on every floor, and kn28's own text reads 'DOORBELL ON/OFF SWITCH (COMMUNICATION FEATURES ROOMS ONLY)'. A100's Guestroom Matrix, floor-1 column, leaves the 'Queen Queen, HI' row BLANK; the single floor-1 hearing-impaired key is 'King Studio, HI | 1 T', i.e. one of 104/106/108/110/112/114. No first-floor Queen-Queen is hearing-accessible, so 105 gets zero. Emitted as a qty-0 confirm-absent line at FLAGGED, origin db-only. Underlying gap: coordination_issues C-04 / placeholder PH-GU-002 — 8 of the 12 HI keys are located (209/213/216/218, 309/313/316/318) and floor 1 has never been scanned for the crossed-ear symbol.

FIRE HORN / HORN-STROBE (A555 keyed note 16) — the DB carries NO notification appliance row for room 105 at all, only the smoke detector. A555 places kn16 on views 04 and 04.1 AND draws the H symbol beside the SD on elevation 06; A550's POWER & SIGNAL LEGEND defines 'ALARM HORN AND STROBE (H)'; kn16 verbatim reads 'FIRE HORN IN STANDARD ROOMS / FIRE HORN/STROBE IN COMMUNICATION FEATURES ROOMS'; and E501–E504 print 'per guestroom: smoke detector + notification'. Against that, FA-2/FA-3 (the Hilton-reviewed vendor submittal) draw NO horn and NO strobe in a standard key. This is simultaneously a DB gap and a live sheet conflict on a device visible from the doorway. Emitted sheets-only at FLAGGED with qty 1 as a placeholder. Precedence points at the submittal, but FA-1's own audibility chart says sleeping rooms are 'visual required'. Recording present/absent in all 16 first-floor rooms closes it.

ACCESS PANEL (min 12"x12") TO THE BATHROOM FIRE DAMPER AND VOLUME DAMPER — no DB row exists. The requirement is printed (M101 GN7 min 12"x12" access to dampers; M301 Key Note 4 access panel above the ceiling for HVAC maintenance; M501 fire-damper access with a permanent exterior label in letters at least 1/2" high) but the placement is missing: none of the ten A550–A556 guestroom RCPs draws one, and A555 view 02's keynotes are only 18, 19, 7, 4 and 1. The bath lid is 7'-3" hard painted gypsum. This is a repeating 115-room omission, an RFI candidate and a CO-inspection exposure — an inspector cannot verify a damper he cannot reach. Emitted sheets-only at FLAGGED. Whatever room 105 shows, expect it in all 16 and on floors 2–4.

INTERIOR ARCHITECTURAL WALL GRILLE AT THE PTAC (M401 KN5) — no DB row. The DB carries only the exterior louver. M401 prints two nearly identical keyed notes, KN1 'painted to match EXTERIOR wall' and KN5 'painted to match INTERIOR wall', and does not say whether that is one grille with two painted faces or two separate grilles. It decides whether there is a separate painted grille inside the finished room to inspect and whose paint scope the room-side face is. Emitted sheets-only at FLAGGED, quantity not stated.

DISHWASHER DISCONNECT SWITCH IN THE CABINET UNDER THE SINK — no DB row. E101 GENERAL NOTE #4 reads verbatim 'Dishwasher switches in cabinet under sink', but it is a set-wide general note with no guestroom placement — no guestroom sheet places a dishwasher-switch keynote or symbol. The dedicated dishwasher circuit itself is certain (A555 kn10, E400 Panel A, E103 1068 VA). Emitted sheets-only at FLAGGED; do not write it up as missing until the EC confirms GN#4 was carried into the guestrooms.

CONNECTED ROOM EDGE CONTROLLER — no DB row. Named twice in A555 kn47 ('PATCH CORD TO EDGE CONTROLLER FOR CONNECTED ROOM', in both option A and option B) and once in E101 GN#8, and appearing nowhere else: no mark, no legend symbol, no E-series schedule, no count, no location. Consistent with the broader condition that no telecom riser diagram, rack elevation, port count or head-end schedule exists anywhere in the set. Emitted sheets-only at FLAGGED.

WIRING DEVICES AND COVER PLATES, GENERAL — no DB row, and mismatched plates is the classic guestroom punch item. E101 spec #14 requires Hubbell devices 'color/style coordinated with architect', GN#2 requires the brand be clarified with the franchise/owner before ordering, and GN#10 requires all receptacles and switches rated 20 A. The ONLY device colour printed anywhere in the set is WHITE, and only at the microwave outlet (A555 kn36). Emitted sheets-only at FLAGGED as a single room-wide check.

TWO ZERO-QUANTITY CONFIRM ROWS the DB does not carry, both emitted sheets-only so the walker neither false-flags an absence nor walks past something unscheduled: (1) NO SPRINKLER HEAD IN THE GUEST BATHROOM — FP-1's room regions for 107 (the same Queen-Queen type as 105) and 108 show no head drawn in either bathroom; recorded as an observation, NOT as an NFPA 13 omission ruling, because the governing standard is itself open (conflicts.md B5.3). Write 'no head drawn', not 'no head required'. (2) NO CARBON MONOXIDE DETECTOR — FA-1 schedules just 3 SKFIRECOW units for the whole 115-key building and places none in a guest room; E500 carries a CO detail but places none; the A550–A556 legend has no CO symbol. This is an ABSENCE, not a verified exclusion — fire-alarm conflict FA-8 asks the AHJ to confirm coverage.

24 DB rows on room 105 are concealed rough-in and were dropped per the scope rule; their punch-visible ends are folded into the lines that remain. ELECTRICAL (13): every branch circuit — Lighting, Convenience Receptacles, Bathroom GFCI, Refrigerator 173 VA, Disposer 480 VA, Dishwasher 1068 VA, Microwave/Hood 850 VA, PTAC 208 V 2080 VA, Small Appliance #1 and #2, Spare — plus the feeder from the floor distribution panel and the PTAC thermostat control-wiring rough-in. All folded into the panelboard line's circuit roll-call. PLUMBING (7): domestic water branch set (1/2" HWR + 3/4" HWS + 1" CWS), fixture runouts, 2" SS waste branch, 3" SS water-closet waste to the 4" stack, vent riser, vent piping, sanitary riser tie — all verified indirectly by the fixtures draining. MECHANICAL (3 plus one partial): 4" fresh-air duct above ceiling, 4" toilet exhaust duct to the EV riser, fire-caulk at rated duct penetrations (named explicitly on Austin's OUT list); and the PTAC field-built sub-base was stripped out of the DB's combined row, leaving only the visible carpet-edge and ST-01 stool checks. NOTE: the thermostat appears in the DB twice — as a Mechanical device row and an Electrical wiring row. The device is emitted ONCE under Mechanical and the wiring dropped, per both extractors' explicit warning not to double-count it.

PTAC MARK ON ROOM 105 — mutually exclusive and unresolved. M301, the only M-sheet carrying floor-1 room numbers, states PTAC-1 at all 16 first-floor guestrooms. M401 detail 01 covers the QQ family (101, 103, 105–115) and calls PTAC-2. M201 schedules them as genuinely different units — AZ65H12DAB at 11,900 BTU/h cooling versus AZ65H15DAB at 14,200 — and M601 COMcheck independently lists them as two compliance items, so the two-units question is settled twice over; only the room assignment is not. M401 KN7 itself defers location to M301–M304, which argues for M301 governing, but M401's own detail contradicts it. No sheet prints the composite string 'PTAC-2 / PTAC-1'; that is the carry-both convention from packages/mechanical.md flag F4. Fastest fix: read the nameplate on the walk.

EF-1 — A REAL IN-ROOM BATH FAN, OR A DESIGNATION FOR A GRILLE INLET ON A CENTRAL RISER? M201 schedules a Panasonic FV-0511VK2 ceiling fan at 50 CFM with remark 3 'switch w/ room lights', and M202/M301–M304 repeat it. M305's riser diagrams show each guestroom inlet as a plain ceiling grille plus an Aldes regulator on a central riser driven by roof fans EF-8 through EF-11, with no in-room fan anywhere. Both cannot be true. E400's Panel A/B guestroom schedules carry no exhaust-fan circuit, which leans grille-only but is not conclusive since remark 3 would put a fan on the Lighting circuit. coordination_issues C-06, a 115-unit buy. Closable by looking behind one bath grille on this walk.

MOUNTING HEIGHTS ARE NOT SETTLED and this is the biggest punch hazard in room 105 — instruct the walker to RECORD every as-built height and write up NONE of them until the RFI returns. Receptacles / data / TV / telephone: 12" AFF (A530 GENERAL NOTES note D, byte-identical on five bath sheets) vs 18" AFF (E101 spec #18, E101 symbol legend, G400 detail 02 'ALL RECEPTACLES SHALL BE 18" A.F.F. UNLESS NOTED OTHERWISE'). Thermostat: 48" (A555 kn24 max-to-top, M101 GN29, G402 note 11, G400) vs 54" (M401 KN4, non-accessible — the only source for it) vs 60" (E101 legend). The one height that IS a hard stated MAX and is enforceable today is the bath switch at 48" to the top of the device (A555 kn3). coordination_issues C-03 / packages/electrical.md open item 1.

SPRINKLER HEAD TRIM — CONCEALED OR SEMI-RECESSED? Two completely different looks from the floor and two different buys. A120/A121 General Note I reads 'SPRINKLER HEADS IN CEILINGS IN PUBLIC AREAS TO BE CONCEALED. ALL OTHER HEADS TO BE SEMI-RECESSED' — a guest room is not a public area, so that note requires semi-recessed in 105. Against it, packages/fire-appliance.md reads FP-1's 'PD' suffix as concealed pendent, which is a reading, not a printed word: FP-1's description column prints only 'VK430 7/16 FR 155 C PD'. The DB's own head descriptions state 'concealed pendent' as fact; the emitted lines carry the printed string instead. Registered as FS-3. Also unstated anywhere in this mirror: cover-plate/escutcheon finish and colour, and the temperature rating — '155' sits inside the model string and FP-1 has no temperature column, so do not put a rating or finish on a purchase document.

FIXTURE-MARK DRIFT ON EVERY GUESTROOM PLUMBING FIXTURE (conflicts.md B3.1, OPEN — both mark sets carried, no winner picked). The enlarged unit plans P401/P402 mark SH-1, L-2, SK-3, SK-4; the P104 schedule lists guestroom showers as SH-3/SH-4, guestroom lavs as L-3/L-4, and only SK-1/SK-2 (both laundry sinks). This costs money, not semantics: P104's own SH-1 is the 36"x36" EMPLOYEE shower (Kohler Sonata K-1689-0) and its L-2 is the EMPLOYEE/POOL wall-hung lav (Decolav Lilac 1819W-1P-CWH with a battery Delta faucet). Order guestroom trim off the plan marks and the wrong pan and the wrong lavatory arrive. Separately, WC-3 vs WC-4 is never assigned per unit type — both print together on the unit plans and no source states which room type gets which (placeholder PH-GU-004).

DOES THE STANDARD GUEST BATH GET A FLOOR DRAIN? P402 places the floor drain in ACCESSIBLE UNITS; A530 keyed note 20 places one on the STANDARD guest-bath plan 01, which is the plan serving room 105 and the other 14 non-accessible first-floor rooms. Both readings carried, neither resolved. Compounding it, the guestroom floor drain has NO MARK AND NO SCHEDULED PRODUCT — P104's Drain and Drainage Appurtenance Schedule carries FD-1 (Mech/Laundry, Zurn Z550), FD-2 (Unfinished Spaces, Zurn Z415B) and FD-3 (Funnel, Zurn Z514E), none of which is a guestroom drain. The trap guard/primer line follows the same answer, and its own two scheduled products (P102 Sioux Chief 695 vs P104 TP-1 PPP SMP-500-115V) are likewise neither of them scoped to a guest bath. Recording present/absent across all 16 baths answers the first question from the field.

PTAC EXTERIOR LOUVER — FIVE STATEMENTS, NO RESOLUTION, spanning material, finish method and which subcontractor buys it. M201: 'polypropylene louver kit (color by architect)'. M501 det.9: 'aluminum architectural-style grille factory-painted to match exterior wall'. M401 KN1: 'architectural wall grille furnished with unit; grille painted to match exterior wall'. A200 keyed note 8 (= AS105 kn 8): 'ALUMINUM FIXED WINDOW WITH THERMAL BROKEN FRAME, INSULATED GLAZING WITH INTEGRAL ALUMINUM LOUVER AT PTAC UNITS' — i.e. part of the window system, the glazing sub's buy, not a PTAC accessory. AS103 corroborates the window-system reading. Polypropylene is moulded in colour and generally cannot be field-painted, so M201's product and M401's paint instruction may be physically incompatible. Compounding: the size reference on A200/AS105 points to sheet A-601, which is NOT in the issued set (the set has A600 Doors and A610 Windows) — RFI R-04 — so the louver has no dimensional source either.

ROOM 105 IS NOT THE ACCESSIBLE ROOM AND NOT THE HEARING-ACCESSIBLE ROOM — stated explicitly because the brief flagged it. A100's text-layer plan label is 'QUEEN QUEEN' and room_map.md joins 105 as room_type Queen-Queen. A100's Guestroom Matrix, floor-1 column, prints 'Queen Queen | 6 S' (105/107/109/111/113/115, all SHOWER), leaves 'Queen Queen, HI' BLANK on floor 1, and shows no QQ accessible key on floor 1 at all. The only accessible key on floor 1 is 118 ('King Studio ACC MOD, CD | 1 T', ISA symbol drawn on the plan); the only hearing-impaired key on floor 1 is a King Studio ('King Studio, HI | 1 T'). CONSEQUENCES FOR 105, all verified absent from both the sheets and the DB and therefore correctly not emitted: no tub BT-1 and no roll-in pan SH-3 (105 is 'S'), no shower diverter kn10, no hand shower and side bar kn11, no accessible-vanity P-trap and supply-line wrap (G402 det 04 / coordination_issues C-09), no 3-way welcome light switch at the bed (G400 det 02, accessible keys only), no motorized-shade switch (105 carries GR-400 MANUAL shades per A555, so no shade circuit and no shade switch), no power-wheelchair outlet, no 15"–48" accessible reach outlet/data requirement (A530 GN G), no ceiling strobes and no doorbell. The one grab bar in 105's bath (HD-08, 24" vertical) is a Bath Accessory row, not MEP, and is already carried in that category.

TWO DB ROWS DELIBERATELY MERGED RATHER THAN EMITTED AS PHANTOM DEVICE LINES, so nothing is silently lost. (1) The PROPOSED LAVATORY SUBSTITUTION row (American Standard Studio bowl 0614.000 / 0614.300 / 0618.000 plus Moen M-Dura 9417F12 / 9419F12 single-hole 1.2 gpm) is not a device to punch — it is a watch instruction, and it is folded into the lavatory faucet line's note and verify step as 'count the deck holes: 3 = Delta as designed, 1 = the unapproved substitution'. It remains NOT APPROVED: the American Standard sheet offers three models with none ticked, the Moen sheet two with neither ticked, no transmittal and no stamp, so it is not a submittal and supersedes nothing (OPEN_ITEMS A3). (2) The three separate GATE VALVE rows (CWS, HWS, HWR) are consolidated into one line at qty 3 with all three services named in the label, because the walker opens one 18"x18" panel and checks three valves in a single action.

SCOPE SEAMS AND DOUBLE-COUNT RISKS the crew must not trip over. (a) The GUESTROOM ENTRY DOOR CARD LOCK (A600 Hardware Set #1, 'Advance Card Lock' on door GR-1) is the only lock or access-control device drawn in any guest room in this set — it is already carried in the DB under the Doors category and is deliberately NOT duplicated in Low Voltage. Punch it once, on the doors walk. (b) The VANITY SCONCE is carried twice by design: electrical fixture WS03 (Arkansas 3550V, E101) and FF&E GR-203 'VANITY SCONE' (A530 kn12). Almost certainly one physical fixture in two packages; no source states the equivalence, so both ride — make sure the FF&E punch and the MEP punch do not both write it up. (c) The FF&E decorative luminaires a walker will switch on in 105 are QQ-specific and are the most commonly mis-ordered guestroom lighting item: GR-207 nightstand sconce @QQ CENTER x1 between the beds plus GR-208 @QQ SIDE x2 outboard — two different SKUs — with GR-204, GR-200, GR-201 and GR-205. They are FF&E rows, not MEP, and are excluded here on purpose. (d) The bi-pass shower door is GLASS SUB scope; PTAC condensate piping is Larry's Plumbing while the PTAC is Iceberg (M401 records this as a frequent interface gap); the thermostat is provided by Iceberg with wiring by United Electric (M101 N28).

THREE DB RELIABILITY GRADES OVERSTATE WHAT THE SHEETS SUPPORT and were downgraded on the emitted lines, each with the reason on the line: PTAC LOUVERED ACCESS PANEL (DB HIGH → FLAGGED: M201 names it in the accessory sentence and nothing else in the mechanical set locates or details it, so whether it is a G.E. unit accessory or an undrawn architectural wall panel is unknown); PTAC LOW-AMBIENT KIT (DB HIGH → MEDIUM: named plainly but no sheet says which component it is or where it can be seen — it is a label/submittal check, not a sight check); ENERGY-MANAGEMENT WALL CONTROLLER (DB HIGH → MEDIUM: M201 names both an EMS controller with occupancy sensor and a 7-day programmable thermostat in one sentence and no mechanical sheet says whether that is one wall device or two). Also downgraded on COUNT rather than identity, per the never-guess rule: S21 bath downlight, extended J-box kn25, and the convenience receptacles — identity is solid in each case but no sheet states a quantity, so qty 1 is a placeholder and the real counts must be read off the E400 / A555 view-04 source PDFs before the walk. ONE MORE THING TO WATCH IN THE FIELD: no ceiling supply diffuser is shown in any guestroom on any mechanical sheet — the PTAC is the supply, and M201's Titus diffuser marks are placed in corridors and public areas. If the walker finds a ceiling supply diffuser in room 105, that is unaccounted for and should be raised.

critic.summary: The product data is clean — every make, model and capacity I spot-checked traces verbatim to P104, M201, E101, M501, P102, P501 or FA-1, and no rough-in leaked back in. The sprinkler count of 3 is right (FP-1 §1.3, room 107, 3 x symbol-dot VK430; the "36 heads / 16 rooms" trap does not apply — FP-1 gives 144 heads on floor 1, 62 of them VK430, so 3 x 16 = 48 leaves a plausible corridor/BOH remainder). The smoke-detector count of 1 is right (FA-1 121/121 = 115 keys + 6 second heads in the one-bedroom suites, none on floor 1). Room-type discipline is correct: A100's floor-1 column reads "Queen Queen | 6 S", the "Queen Queen, HI" row is blank, and the sole floor-1 HI key is a King Studio — so no tub, no roll-in, no diverter, no hand shower, no strobes, no doorbell, no motorised shade and no welcome switch, all correctly excluded. Verify steps are real actions throughout. But the list fails on three counts. (1) It omits a device the walker touches in every room: there is no line for the entry / closet / general room light switch, and consequently no line carries the three-value switch-height conflict (G400 det 02 = 3'-10", E101 spec #18 = 54", E101 legend = 48"; conflicts.md #5 / coordination_issues C-03). (2) It misses a live sheet conflict on bath-fan switching — G402 general note 3 requires the fan switched SEPARATELY from the light, M201 EF-1 remark 3 says "switch w/ room lights" — which decides whether there is a second switch in the bath. (3) It carries four false or misattributed citations, including "A555 KN30", a keynote that is not placed anywhere on A555. That is exactly the failure the iron rules exist to stop. Fix the twelve items below and it is a good walk sheet.
missingDevices: Entry / closet / general room light switch(es) — no line exists; E400's own systems list prints "switching (entry, bath w/ integrated night light)" and G400 detail 02 schedules a SWITCH height of 3'-10" (UNO)

Bathroom exhaust-fan switch — a second bath switch exists if G402 general note 3 governs ("CEILING MOUNTED LIGHT FIXTURE AND FAN TO BE SWITCHED SEPARATELY FROM LIGHT") rather than M201 EF-1 remark 3 ("switch w/ room lights")

Ceiling supply diffuser — zero-quantity confirm line; the reconciler's own note says an unaccounted diffuser found in 105 must be raised, but no line carries it while five other qty-0 confirm lines were emitted
Trap guard TG-1 — the only trap-guard mark printed in the set (P104 drainage schedule, on FD-1 / FD-2 / FS) is not carried on the trap-guard line

defects.line: Mechanical — "PTAC exterior louver / architectural wall grille kit — material NOT settled"
defects.problem: This line is not verifiable at punch under Austin's own scope rule. Its `where` field says "read from outside the building" and its verify step says "From outside, record the material actually installed … and colour-matched down the whole elevation." That is a facade walk on a 4-storey building, not a person standing in a finished guest room. The list correctly flags the five-way material conflict, but it never flags that the ITEM ITSELF is an arguable scope call — and the rule for arguable calls (put it IN and mark needsRuling=true with the argument) was applied to the fire damper, the volume damper and the gate valves but not here.
defects.correction: Set needsRuling=true and state the argument: "AGAINST: not visible, touchable or testable from inside the finished room — this is an exterior elevation check. FOR: it is the room's own PTAC assembly and nobody else is carrying it." Either move it to an exterior/facade punch with a cross-reference on the room sheet, or keep it IN with the ruling flag. The interior grille line (M401 KN5) is correctly scoped and stays.

defects.line: Plumbing — "SH-1 / SH-4 Shower, guestroom … 105 IS A SHOWER ROOM, CONFIRMED" (reliability HIGH)
defects.problem: The claim is almost certainly right, but a printed contradiction on the governing sheet is left unrecorded. A555 view 02 (the QQ reflected ceiling plan) places keynote 7, and keynote 7 in the shared 44-note legend reads "BATHTUB." A550's RCP for the King Studio places 18, 19, 4 and 1 with no 7. The iron rule is that where two sheets disagree, both readings are recorded and flagged — not resolved silently. This is the same sheet the list relies on for kn18, kn19 and the ceiling heights, so its keynote list cannot be trusted selectively.
defects.correction: Keep the shower at HIGH on A100's matrix ("Queen Queen | 6 S", floor 1) and A530 ("The standard guest bath is a SHOWER, not a tub"), and add to the instanceNote: "RECORDED, NOT RESOLVED — A555 view 02, the QQ RCP that governs 105, places keynote 7 = BATHTUB; A550's King Studio RCP does not. Reads as a drafting carry-over, but it is printed on the governing sheet. Confirm no tub rough-in exists behind the SS-01 surround."
